A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LIFT. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison, including Appendices A-H in v4 and A-K in v5.

before.justification: V4 reports original SQuAD, NIAH and LooGLE experiments, efficiency measurements, and appendix evaluations of retained capabilities and method variants.

after.justification: V5 retains these original results and adds synthetic-data diversity, target-model generation, summarization and mathematical skill-acquisition experiments in Appendices I-K.

M1.justification: The core LIFT objective and asynchronous pipeline remain unchanged. Appendix K adds task-specific adaptations: fine-tuning on summaries at multiple granularities, and generating training data through reasoning-step rewrites and analogous mathematical examples.

E1.justification: Appendix K adds GovReport summarization and a GSM8K scenario that adapts the model to solved examples before testing an unseen problem. This substantially extends evaluated task requirements. V4 already used GSM8K in Appendix G, but only to assess general capabilities after adaptation to LooGLE documents; that evaluation is retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the retained comparisons, including MemoryLLM, LlamaIndex, TempLoRA, LLMLingua, Finetune-Raw, truncated ICL, SEAL and LLoCO. The new generator and task-extension experiments reuse the existing ICL baseline.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce QA-format and content-category training controls, a Llama-3-8B generator configuration, and a GSM8K protocol using ten solved examples followed by an unseen test problem. These are additional experimental settings; the stated protocols and budgets of retained experiments are unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix I adds experiments restricting synthetic tasks to a uniform 'what-is' format or individual content categories, alongside a category distribution and examples. Appendix J tests whether the target model can generate useful training tasks itself. These substantially extend analysis of two central dependencies: synthetic-data diversity and generator strength.

E5.justification: Appendix G retains averaging over ten models adapted to different LooGLE documents. V5 adds no seed information, repeated-run counts, uncertainty intervals or significance-testing procedures; the new tables report point estimates.

E6.justification: Existing matched results are unchanged, but Tables 11-13 add substantial findings. The target-generator experiment reports 48.49/26.93 for ShortQA/LongQA. Table 13 reports LIFT versus ICL scores of 30.9 versus 29.1 on GovReport and 65.4 versus 57.6 on GSM8K. These are newly reported experiments, not improvements over corresponding v4 results; Table 13 leaves its metrics unnamed.

T1.justification: Equation (1)'s synthetic-task objective and Section 3.3's O(ml²) versus O(m²l²) complexity argument are unchanged. V5 introduces no new formal assumptions, propositions, proofs or mathematical derivations.

C1.justification: The introduction adds an explicit contribution claim extending LIFT beyond long-context comprehension to in-context skill acquisition. The abstract, principal context-in-parameters claims and conclusion remain unchanged.

C2.justification: New passages interpret diversity as beneficial, argue that LIFT does not critically require a strong generator, and attribute the GSM8K results to learning reasoning patterns. Related work also argues that training can internalize abstract heuristics that RAG struggles to retrieve. The existing limitation concerning cross-document information association remains unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendices I-K document new filtering and rewriting procedures, generator choices, three summaries per twenty sentences, and ten analogous problems per solved example. Existing hyperparameters, hardware descriptions, prompts and code-access information remain unchanged. Appendix K does not specify evaluation metrics, sample counts or splits.

R1.justification: V5 adds Huang et al. (2021) for GovReport and expands its positioning against RAG with examples involving abstract rules and reasoning heuristics. The remaining cited works and broader research positioning are retained.

P1.justification: V5 adds an introductory contribution bullet, expands the RAG discussion and appends Sections I-K. Several cross-references change from 'Section' to 'Appendix'. These are localized additions and edits within the existing narrative and section order.

P2.justification: V5 adds Figure 7 and Tables 11-13, reorders the LongQA subtask columns in Table 3, and relocates existing displays through page reflow. Table 7's caption changes from QuALITY to LooGLE, matching the experiment already described in both versions. Existing figure content is retained.

improvement.justification: V5 strengthens empirical support by examining synthetic-data diversity and demonstrating useful adaptation with the target model as generator, dependencies not directly tested in v4. Task-extension results and the corrected Table 7 caption also help. The overall gain is limited by Appendix K's unspecified metrics, sample counts and splits, and Appendix I's lack of documented controls for training-data volume.
